subject: gk
question: Green Revolution was mainly for which crops?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat and Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India primarily focused on the cultivation of **wheat and rice**.
 
• It began in the 1960s with the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds.
 
• Norman Borlaug, an American agronomist, is often credited with the development and spread of these high-yielding wheat seeds.
 
• MS Swaminathan played a key role in bringing the Green Revolution to India, making the country self-sufficient in food grains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYV)**

 
 
• These are seeds developed to increase the productivity of crops.
 
• HYV seeds are often resistant to diseases and pests.
 
• They require more water and fertilizers compared to traditional seeds.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Farmers**
 
 
• The Green Revolution increased the income of farmers who adopted HYV seeds.
 
• It led to regional disparities, benefiting mainly the Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh regions.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns**
 
 
• Excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides has led to soil degradation.
 
• Overuse of water resources for irrigation has resulted in water scarcity in some areas.
 
 
 
• **Food Security**
 
 
• The Green Revolution played a crucial role in making India self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• It helped in reducing India's dependence on food imports.
